recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit as-is; no follow-up source work is recommended for FHIR-8683 unless a future work-group decision reopens the broader HTTP/HTTPS identity policy.
issue_request: FHIR-8683 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core change request against FHIR-core-http asking to replace the unclear statement that "http:" and "https:" are exchangeable and refer to the same object with language saying they must not be used to refer to different resources/objects.
initial_application: FHIR-5512 introduced the original HTTP/HTTPS and port identity guidance in source/http.html in git-svn commit d0f47223ad0f368f159e7f2ccbd205234b2fc31f. FHIR-8683 was applied as QA in git-svn commit cd02a83cb81e816388e258b698d29f8f9b4c49ee, which removed the "exchangeable" sentence and replaced it with the current SHALL NOT wording.
additional_context: The authoritative current source page is source/http.html. Its Identity section preserves the FHIR-5512 port distinction while clarifying that HTTP and HTTPS variants need not both be served, treated the same, or have identical content. Jira searches for the original phrase found only FHIR-8683 and FHIR-5512, and Zulip/Confluence searches found no relevant conflicting evidence.
reconciliation: No source edit was made. The current source already implements the FHIR-8683 clarification and does not contain the ambiguous "exchangeable" wording.
